Nevada is a very diverse state that has a little of everything. Las Vegas is obviously the largest city, and although the population is relatively small at about 2 million it has everything you'd expect to find in a city several times its size. It's also basically "open" 24/7/365 and there's lots to do. One of the most underrated aspects of Las Vegas is the proximity to nature. Red Rock Canyon has beautiful desert hiking, but Mt. Charleston is only about half an hour from the strip and is at a high enough elevation that the forest and wildlife will make you think you're somewhere else entirely. Zion and Bryce Canyon are also only a few hours away in Utah, close enough for a day trip.

Reno is another great city, although it's nowhere near as large as Las Vegas and it can be a little rural. Still, like Las Vegas, it has amenities that you normally wouldn't find in a city of its size and it feels much bigger than it actually is in that respect. Reno and Vegas have a lot in common, but Reno is definitely more conservative than Vegas and more family-friendly.

Lake Tahoe is about an hour from Reno, and it's an absolutely magical place. The lake is a beautiful shade of blue and its got some of the most beautiful hiking in the world. Its surrounded by mountains, and has some of the best skiing you'll ever find. The Nevada side is fairly conservative and the people are generally very friendly. There are lots of smaller towns surrounding the lake, each with its own unique charms. Although it definitely seems very remote at times, Reno and Carson City are still close enough that you're not missing too much by not being in a big city.
